sections.html:
On the South Shore, Weymouth is a Norfolk County city with Hingham Bay and Boston Harbor along its northern edge. It covers 21.58 square miles, of which 4.81 are water, and the 2020 census counted 57,437 residents. Quincy, Braintree and Holbrook lie to the west, Abington and Rockland to the south and Hingham to the east. The city keeps "Town of Weymouth" as its official name, though voters replaced town meeting with a mayor and council in 1999, and the first mayor took office in 2000.

The city began in 1622 as the Wessagusset colony and took the Weymouth name in 1635, making it the second-oldest settlement in Massachusetts after Plymouth. Shoemaking was the main industry from the early 1700s until Stetson Shoe closed in 1973.

Residents describe four districts, and buyers shop by them.

  • North Weymouth sits north of the Church, North and Green Street junction and has the waterfront parks and beaches.
  • South Weymouth lies mostly south of Route 3 and holds Weymouth High School and South Shore Hospital.
  • East Weymouth has Whitman's Pond, Jackson Square and Town Hall, plus many Victorian houses.
  • Weymouth Landing spans about a mile around Weston Park at the Braintree line.

Union Point is the redevelopment of the former Naval Air Station South Weymouth, which closed in the 1990s. Plans include a parkway, residences, a sports facility and a movie studio, and the 25-acre Union Point Sports Complex is already open. Great Esker Park, George Lane Beach and Webb Memorial State Park are in North Weymouth.

Water shapes much of Weymouth, from Hingham Bay to the Back River and Fore River. The city is especially vulnerable to sea level rise, and North Weymouth waterfront cottages are being bought and rebuilt, so condition and flood exposure vary a great deal from street to street. Average precipitation runs about 44 inches a year.

If you own near the shore:

  • Pull your flood insurance policy and any elevation certificate.
  • Document sea wall, bulkhead or drainage repairs with dates.
  • Tell buyers, including a cash buyer, about past water in the basement.

Put the history in writing for any buyer, since hiding it tends to surface at inspection.

East Weymouth has many Queen Anne, shingle and colonial revival houses, with restoration under way on streets such as Hillcrest Road. Whatever the village, have the roof, heating system, wiring and porches looked at before you decide how to sell.

If you inherited one of these houses and live elsewhere, a repair list can be the biggest hurdle to a traditional listing, and that is a common reason owners pick a cash sale.

South Weymouth is home to Weymouth High School, the only public high school, with more than 1,800 students. The Maria Weston Chapman Middle School opened in September 2022, and eight primary schools and an early childhood center complete the system. Private options include South Shore Christian Academy and the Catholic Sacred Heart and St. Francis Xavier schools.

Routes 3, 3A, 18, 53, 58 and 139 pass through the city. The MBTA Greenbush Line stops at East Weymouth and Weymouth Landing/East Braintree, and the Kingston Line stops at South Weymouth. If your house is within reach of a station, say so in any listing.

sections.h2: How Massachusetts abatements work for Weymouth owners
sections.html:
Abatement requests in Weymouth run on state rules. The grounds are an assessment above fair cash value on the January 1 valuation date, or an exemption or classification that was missed.

  • Quarterly bills usually fall due on August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1.
  • Your abatement application must be in by the first installment date, generally February 1 for such cities.
  • The assessors get three months, and silence is a denial.
  • After that, three months remain to appeal to the Appellate Tax Board.

Weymouth's assessing office can tell you which billing pattern applies and hand you the form.

ChargeAmount
Deed recording fee, recorded land$156
Deed excise tax$2.28 for each $500 of the stated price
Municipal lien certificate$81
Mortgage discharge$106 per marginal reference

Weymouth deeds are recorded with the Norfolk County Registry of Deeds. The excise must be paid with an attorney's check or bank check. Budget for the small items too.

1. Collect the latest tax bill, any flood insurance policy, repair receipts and lease copies for tenants.
  2. Decide whether to list, sell privately or take a cash offer.
  3. Ask the assessing office which billing schedule applies, and note any open balance.
  4. Hire an attorney, who coordinates the deed, the payoff of any mortgage and the recording in Norfolk County.
  5. Pay the excise tax by attorney's check or bank check when the deed is recorded.
  6. Sign, close and hand over the keys.

Money owed in taxes or liens comes out of your proceeds when the sale closes, so request payoff figures before accepting. Then every offer can be judged by your real take-home.

Cash buyers study the address, the shape of the house and any liens, then put a number in writing. Take it, and a title company or attorney drafts the documents while you pick the closing day. Open houses disappear, and so does the long wait on a buyer's loan and the repair demands a lender's inspection can bring. The deed, the excise tax and the recording do not change.

Because the buyer inherits the repairs, a roof, porch or heating system you would otherwise fix before listing becomes part of the price discussion. For a waterfront cottage or a Victorian with deferred upkeep, that swap can be worth making.

Whether the buyer pays cash or uses a loan, tell them what you know about the house. For a shoreline property that means flood history, sea wall or bulkhead work and any basement water. For an East Weymouth Victorian it means the age of the roof, wiring, heating and porches. If tenants live there, share the lease terms. Written notes protect you, and a cash buyer who sees them early can make a firmer offer with fewer conditions.

A short folder with dates and receipts is usually enough, and it keeps the closing attorney from having to chase you for paperwork in the final week.

sections.h2: Cash sale versus listing for a Weymouth house
sections.html:
Homes near the commuter rail can draw plenty of interest on the market, though showings and repairs eat time. Cash tends to suit owners on a tight schedule, heirs, and anyone staring at a repair bill they would rather not pay.

Whoever the buyer is, request proof of funds, a written contract and a plain statement of who pays each closing cost, then compare what you would net each way.

faqs.q: Is Weymouth, MA a city or a town?
faqs.a: Weymouth has a city form of government but keeps "Town of Weymouth" as its official name. Voters replaced town meeting with a mayor and council in 1999.

faqs.q: How many train stations are in Weymouth?
faqs.a: Three. The Greenbush Line stops at East Weymouth and Weymouth Landing/East Braintree, and the Kingston Line stops at South Weymouth.

faqs.q: How much is the deed excise tax in Norfolk County?
faqs.a: $2.28 for each $500 of the stated price, with any fraction of $500 counted in full, due at recording by attorney's check or bank check.

faqs.q: Which parts of Weymouth are near the water?
faqs.a: North Weymouth faces Hingham Bay and Boston Harbor. The Back River and Fore River also run through the city, so check flood exposure street by street.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Weymouth house as is?
faqs.a: Yes. An investor or cash buyer can purchase it in its current condition. Put known problems in writing, and expect a lower offer to match the repairs.
